~/.config/opencode/opencode.json

└── packages/

### Find instances with SelectorOptions examples

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-code-connect/references/api.md

Usage examples for finding instances by specific hierarchy path or traversing all nested instances.

```javascript
// Find icon only in specific hierarchy
const icon = instance.findInstance('Icon', {
  path: ['Header', 'Actions', 'IconSlot']
})

// Search everywhere including nested instances
const anyIcon = instance.findInstance('Icon', {
  traverseInstances: true
})
```

### Return a cleanup function from setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

Return a cleanup function for resources owned by the plugin. The example registers a listener with context.data.on and returns a function that stops it.

```typescript
setup(context) {
  const stop = context.data.on("session.execution.succeeded", () => {})
  return () => stop()
}
```

### Create an OpenCode client and start a session

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/client/index.mdx

Instantiate an OpenCode client with OpenCode.make and invoke resource methods like session.create and session.prompt.

```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/client"

const client = OpenCode.make({
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:4096",
})

const session = await client.session.create({
  location: { directory: "/workspace" },
})

await client.session.prompt({
  sessionID: session.id,
  text: "Review the current changes",
})
```

### Install OpenCode via curl, npm, Homebrew, pacman, paru, mise, or Nix

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/README.md

Install OpenCode using the YOLO script or a package manager. Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.

```bash
# YOLO
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash

# Package managers
npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest      # or bun/pnpm/yarn
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2 # macOS and Linux (recommended, always up to date)
brew install opencode              # macOS and Linux (official brew formula, updated less)
sudo pacman -S opencode            # Arch Linux (Stable)
paru -S opencode-beta              # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
mise use -g opencode               # Any OS
nix run github:anomalyco/opencode  # Nix
```

### Define a Setup Function for a Desktop Extension

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-extensions/README.md

Use this setup function to register a settings page and command for a desktop extension. It lazily loads the page while idle and only shows remote access and screen active settings when pairing is active.

```tsx
import { lazy, onCleanup, Suspense } from "solid-js"
import { onIdle, Command, SettingsPage, type Setup } from "../sdk"
import type definition from "./index"

const setup: Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.desktop) return
  const layout = ctx.layout
  const servers = ctx.servers
  const pairing = ctx.uses.pairing
  const Page = lazy(() => import("./page"))
  // Settings rows are small; load them while idle so settings opens without a blank row.
  onCleanup(onIdle(() => void Page.preload()))

  // The desktop's own server. Its ref is already authenticated in this window, so codes need no main process.
  const local = () =>
    servers
      .list()
      .map((id) => servers.get(id))
      .find((server) => server?.builtin)

  ctx.add(SettingsPage, {
    id: "pairing",
    icon: "server",
    available: "desktop",
    get title() {
      return ctx.t("title")
    },
    get entries() {
      const pairingEntry = { id: "pairing", title: ctx.t("title"), keywords: "pair device qr phone remote" }

      // Remote access and the display setting exist only while pairing's main side answers.
      if (pairing().status !== "active") return [pairingEntry]

      return [
        pairingEntry,
        {
          id: "settings-remote-access",
          title: ctx.t("remote.title"),
          description: ctx.t("remote.description"),
          keywords: "internet tunnel opentunnel",
        },
        {
          id: "settings-keep-screen-active",
          title: ctx.t("screenActive.title"),
          description: ctx.t("screenActive.description"),
          keywords: "display sleep awake local",
        },
      ]
    },
    render: () => (
      <Suspense>
        <Page server={local} pairing={pairing} />
      </Suspense>
    ),
  })

  ctx.add(Command, {
    id: "open",
    get title() {
      return ctx.t("command.title")
    },
    get group() {
      return ctx.t("command.category.server")
    },
    run: () => layout.settings("pairing"),
  })
}

export default setup
```

### Starting and connecting to a local service instance with Service.ensure

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/client/index.mdx

Imports the native Promise service API and initializes an OpenCode client connected to a running or newly started background service.

```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/client"
import { Service } from "@opencode/client/service"

const endpoint = await Service.ensure()
const client = OpenCode.make({
  baseUrl: endpoint.url,
  headers: Service.headers(endpoint),
})

const info = await client.server.info()
```

--------------------------------

### Initial load and background plugin boot flow

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/specs/v2/catalog-config-plugin-lifecycle.md

Illustrates building a baseline catalog from immediate sources while background fibers activate slower plugins asynchronously.

```ts
LocationServiceMap.get(ref)
  → build location layer
    → Catalog.layer creates empty catalog state
    → PluginBoot.layer activates immediately available plugins
      → ConfigProviderPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → ModelsDevPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → AuthPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
    → Catalog.layer applies active transforms during boot
    → apply policy
    → materialize baseline provider/model catalog
  → PluginBoot baseline ready
    → Frontend.fetchCatalog()

PluginBoot background fiber
  → install/update plugin packages concurrently
  → activate completed plugins
    → Catalog.transform()
      → transform(updateCatalog)
        → Catalog internally rebuilds
          → Catalog.Event.Updated
            → Frontend.refetchCatalog()
```

### Access context properties in setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

The setup function receives configuration, app metadata, the current location, the OpenCode client, cached data, theme tokens, the OpenTUI renderer, and UI APIs. Use context.options, context.location, context.app, context.client, context.renderer, and context.theme to access these values.

```typescript
setup(context) {
  const compact = context.options.compact === true
  const location = context.location ?? context.data.location.default()
  const version = context.app.version
  const channel = context.app.channel
  const client = context.client
  const renderer = context.renderer
  const theme = context.theme
}
```

--------------------------------

### Build and run desktop startup benchmarks

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/desktop/README.md

Builds the desktop application with electron-builder and executes startup benchmark commands under various configurations, such as warm/cold services, A/B comparisons, and profiling flags.

```bash
OPENCODE_CHANNEL=dev bun run build && bunx electron-builder --win --dir --config electron-builder.config.ts
bun run bench:startup -- --runs 5                                  # warm service (started once, reused by every launch)
bun run bench:startup -- --runs 5 --compare dist/other/OpenCode\ Dev.exe   # A/B: alternate launches of two builds
bun run bench:startup -- --service cold                            # each launch spawns the service
bun run bench:startup -- --fresh                                   # first launch after an install (profile wiped each time)
bun run bench:startup -- --profile-main --profile-renderer --trace # CPU profiles and a Chromium startup trace
bun run bench:startup -- --seed "%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop.dev"   # restore tabs and drafts from an existing profile
```

### Set environment variables for an LSP server with env

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/lsp.mdx

Use the `env` property to set environment variables when starting the LSP server. The example sets `RUST_LOG` to `debug` for rust-analyzer.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "lsp": {
    "rust": {
      "command": ["rust-analyzer"],
      "env": {
        "RUST_LOG": "debug"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Return a cleanup function in plugin setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/README.md

Returns a cleanup callback from setup that OpenCode awaits when the plugin is unloaded or replaced.

```ts
setup: async (ctx) => {
  const timer = setInterval(refresh, 60_000)
  return () => clearInterval(timer)
}
```

### Setup function using ctx.uses, ctx.stores, and ctx.add

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-extensions/README.md

Access optional dependencies via ctx.uses and declared stores via ctx.stores. Contribute to a registry with ctx.add.

```ts
const setup: Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  const changes = ctx.uses.changes // Accessor<Live<Changes>>
  const prefs = ctx.stores.prefs.value // loaded before setup
  ctx.add(Command, { id: "open", title: ctx.t("open"), run: () => ctx.layout.settings(ctx.id) })
}
```

### Configuring Service.ensure with custom registration and compatibility options

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/client/index.mdx

Customizes the registration file path, version compatibility predicate, start command, and start lifecycle callback for `Service.ensure()`.

```ts
const endpoint = await Service.ensure({
  file: "/var/run/opencode/service.json",
  version: (version) => version.startsWith("2."),
  command: ["opencode", "serve", "--service"],
  onStart(reason, previousVersion) {
    console.log(reason, previousVersion)
  },
})
```

```typescript
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "example",
  async setup(ctx) {
    await ctx.storage.set("loaded", true)
  },
})
```

### TextNode Range Methods

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-use-figjam/references/edit-text.md

SDK methods on TextNode for getting and setting properties across a specific character range (start to end indices).

```APIDOC
## TextNode Range Methods

### Description
Methods available on `TextNode` instances to apply mixed styling, fonts, fills, hyperlinks, and list options to specific character ranges.

### Methods
- `textNode.setRangeFontName(start, end, fontName)`
- `textNode.setRangeFontSize(start, end, size)`
- `textNode.setRangeFills(start, end, fills)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextDecoration(start, end, decoration)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextCase(start, end, textCase)`
- `textNode.setRangeLetterSpacing(start, end, spacing)`
- `textNode.setRangeLineHeight(start, end, lineHeight)`
- `textNode.setRangeHyperlink(start, end, hyperlink)`
- `textNode.setRangeListOptions(start, end, listOptions)`
- `textNode.setRangeIndentation(start, end, indentation)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontName(start, end)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontSize(start, end)`

### Usage Examples
```javascript
// Make "Hello" bold (characters 0-5)
textNode.setRangeFontName(0, 5, { family: 'Inter', style: 'Bold' });

// Make "World" red (characters 6-11)
textNode.setRangeFills(6, 11, [{ type: 'SOLID', color: { r: 1, g: 0, b: 0 } }]);

// Change size of "World"
textNode.setRangeFontSize(6, 11, 24);

// Get properties for a range
const fontAtStart = textNode.getRangeFontName(0, 1);
const sizeAtEnd = textNode.getRangeFontSize(10, 11);
```
```

### OpenCode.make(options)

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/client/index.mdx

Instantiates a new OpenCode client instance configured with the server URL, optional default headers, and a custom fetch implementation.

```APIDOC
## OpenCode.make(options)

### Description
Creates and configures an OpenCode client instance to communicate with an OpenCode server.

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Configuration options for the client.
  - **baseUrl** (string) - Base URL of the OpenCode server.
  - **headers** (object, optional) - Default HTTP headers included with requests (e.g., authorization).
  - **fetch** (function, optional) - Custom fetch implementation.

### Example
```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/client"

const client = OpenCode.make({
  baseUrl: "http://localhost:4096",
  headers: {
    authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OPENCODE_TOKEN}`,
  },
})
```
```

--------------------------------

### Register and invoke RPC in plugin setup (src/index.ts)

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/rpc.mdx

Registers an RPC implementation inside plugin `setup` using `ctx.rpc.register`, handles cancellation via `context.signal`, returns errors with `context.error`, calls the registered RPC, and emits custom events.

```ts
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"
import { Acme } from "./rpc.js"

export default Plugin.define({
  id: "acme-plugin",
  async setup(ctx) {
    const registration = await ctx.rpc.register(Acme, {
      search: async (input, context) => {
        const { query } = input as { query: string }
        const text = await findText(query, { signal: context.signal })
        if (!text) return context.error("not_found", "Result not found", { query })
        return { text }
      },
    })

    const acme = ctx.rpc(Acme)
    const result = await acme.search({ query: "hello" })

    await registration.events.emit("updated", { itemID: "item-1", text: "ready" })
  },
})
```

### Call keymap.layer from async setup after await

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

Call `layer` from `setup`, including after an `await`, or from a component. The layer factory must be pure; OpenCode evaluates it once without dependency tracking to validate the initial command shape, then reactively.

```ts
async setup(context) {
  const settings = await loadSettings()
  context.keymap.layer(() => ({
    mode: "global",
    commands: [{ id: "acme.sync", title: "Sync Acme", palette: true, run: () => sync(settings) }],
  }))
}
```

### Define project instructions in AGENTS.md

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/ar/rules.mdx

An example AGENTS.md file configuring project structure, code standards, and monorepo conventions for an SST v3 project.

```markdown
# SST v3 Monorepo Project

This is an SST v3 monorepo with TypeScript. The project uses bun workspaces for package management.

## Project Structure

- `packages/` - Contains all workspace packages (functions, core, web, etc.)
- `infra/` - Infrastructure definitions split by service (storage.ts, api.ts, web.ts)
- `sst.config.ts` - Main SST configuration with dynamic imports

## Code Standards

- Use TypeScript with strict mode enabled
- Shared code goes in `packages/core/` with proper exports configuration
- Functions go in `packages/functions/`
- Infrastructure should be split into logical files in `infra/`

## Monorepo Conventions

- Import shared modules using workspace names: `@my-app/core/example`
```

    "thinking": "hide",
    "grouping": "auto",

### Configure Atomic Chat local provider in opencode.json

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx

Use this to connect opencode to a local Atomic Chat server via its OpenAI-compatible API. The baseURL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1; change the host and port to match your setup. Each model ID must match an id returned by GET /v1/models.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "atomic-chat": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Atomic Chat (local)",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1"
      },
      "models": {
        "<your-model-id>": {
          "name": "<your-model-name>"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

{
  "base": {

    }

  "light": {

### Start video generation and stream events with ai.video.start

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/ai/README.md

Use ai.video.start to create a generation handle, then iterate its events with a polling interval. The handle's status and progress are snapshots; call refresh() to get a new handle. Every promise method and stream accepts { signal }; aborting rejects the Promise or throws from the for await loop with signal.reason, while break stops a stream without throwing.

```typescript
import { ai } from "@opencode/ai"

const generation = await ai.video.start({ model, prompt })
for await (const event of generation.events({ poll: { interval: 10_000 } })) console.log(event.type)
const video = await generation.result({ signal })
await ai.write(video.video, "./kite.mp4")
```

### Automatically review pull requests with OpenCode

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/github.mdx

Use this workflow to automatically review PRs when they are opened or updated. If no `prompt` is provided, OpenCode defaults to reviewing the pull request. `issues: write` lets OpenCode react to and comment on the PR, since GitHub handles PR comments through the issues API. This example is intended for PRs from branches in the same repository; PRs from forks normally get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and no secrets.

```yaml
name: opencode-review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: anomalyco/opencode/github@latest
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
          use_github_token: true
          prompt: |
            Review this pull request:
            - Check for code quality issues
            - Look for potential bugs
            - Suggest improvements
```

### Create a SKILL.md file for a git-release skill

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/skills.mdx

```markdown
---
name: Git Release
description: Prepare release notes, version bumps, and GitHub releases
---

## Workflow

1. Read `references/release-policy.md`.
2. Summarize merged changes since the previous tag.
3. Propose the version bump before changing files.
4. Run `scripts/changelog.ts` only after the user approves the version.
```

### Customize OpenCode instance with plugins

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/sdk/index.mdx

Define and register plugins at startup using OpenCode.create() to customize agents, models, and tools. Additional plugins can also be registered after startup via opencode.plugin().

```ts
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/sdk"

const plugin = Plugin.define({
  id: "customize-agent",
  async setup(ctx) {
    await ctx.agent.transform((agents) => {
      agents.update("build", (agent) => {
        agent.description = "Builds features and fixes bugs for our team"
      })
    })
  },
})

await using opencode = await OpenCode.create({ plugins: [plugin] })
```

gantt
    title Q1 Launch Plan

    Synthesis       :done, s1, after r1, 1w

### View serve help with opencode serve --help

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/cli/commands.mdx

Displays all subcommands and flags for the serve command.

```bash
$ opencode serve --help
```

--------------------------------

### GET /session/status

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx

Get session status for all sessions. Returns an object mapping session IDs to SessionStatus.

```APIDOC
## GET /session/status

### Description
Get session status for all sessions.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/session/status

### Response
#### Success Response (200)
- **{ [sessionID: string]: SessionStatus }** - Object mapping session IDs to SessionStatus
```

### GET /config

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx

Retrieves configuration information. Use this endpoint to get the current server or application configuration.

```APIDOC
## GET /config

### Description
Get config info.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/config

### Response
#### Success Response
- **Config** (object) - The configuration information

#### Response Example
{
  // Config object
}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure instructions in opencode.jsonc

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/instructions.mdx

Specifies instruction sources including local files, globs, home directory paths, and remote URLs. Configured instructions load in order after AGENTS.md files.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "instructions": [
    "CONTRIBUTING.md",
    "docs/guidelines/*.md",
    "~/rules/opencode.md",
    "https://example.com/instructions.md",
  ],
}
```

### Run /connect and Select Other Provider

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx

Start the /connect command and scroll down to select the Other provider option to add a custom OpenAI-compatible provider.

```bash
$ /connect

┌  Add credential
│
◆  Select provider
│  ...
│  ● Other
└
```

### Run desktop startup benchmark with custom sample count

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/app/e2e/performance/README.md

Overrides the run count for targeted startup diagnostics using the DESKTOP_STARTUP_RUNS environment variable.

```sh
DESKTOP_STARTUP_RUNS=1 bun run bench:devex
```

--------------------------------

### Execute the /update slash command

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/tui.mdx

Check for a new version of OpenCode and install it. If a newer OpenCode 1 release is available, the dialog installs it. If OpenCode 1 is up to date, it offers to upgrade you to OpenCode 2 instead. OpenCode never installs updates on its own.

```bash
/update
```

--------------------------------

### Preview uninstallation with --dry-run

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/cli/index.mdx

Previews the files and installation components that will be cleaned up prior to actual removal. Session data, configuration, and state are preserved.

```bash
opencode uninstall --dry-run
```

Install the Effect-native OpenCode client and the required Effect version.

```sh
bun add @opencode/client effect@4.0.1
```

### Support V1 and V2 from one package with Plugin.define and server()

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/migrate-v1.mdx

A package can temporarily expose both implementations from one default export. V1 calls `server()` and V2 calls `setup()`; the APIs remain separate and this shape does not translate hooks automatically. V1 object entrypoints are supported in OpenCode `1.18.29` and newer.

```ts
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default {
  ...Plugin.define({
    id: "example",
    async setup(ctx) {
      await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      })
    },
  }),
  async server() {
    return {
      "tool.execute.before": async () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      },
    }
  },
}
```

### GET /provider/auth

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx

Retrieves provider authentication methods. Use this endpoint to get the available authentication methods for each provider.

```APIDOC
## GET /provider/auth

### Description
Get provider authentication methods.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/provider/auth

### Response
#### Success Response
- **{ [providerID: string]: ProviderAuthMethod[] }** (object) - A mapping of provider IDs to their authentication methods

#### Response Example
{
  "providerID": [
    // ProviderAuthMethod objects
  ]
}
```

### Run subagent-eviction.ts with DEMO_LABEL=AFTER

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/script/drive/subagent-eviction.md

Executes the subagent eviction proof script using opencode-drive to assert successful delivery after parent location eviction and rebuild. Requires Bun 1.4.2, opencode-drive 2.1.3, and an installed V2 checkout.

```sh
OPENCODE_DRIVE_DB=proof.sqlite \
OPENCODE_DRIVE_MEDIA_DIR=$PWD/.drive-output \
DEMO_LABEL=AFTER \
opencode-drive run script/drive/subagent-eviction.ts

```

### Get and set focused slide on PageNode

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-use-slides/references/slide-properties.md

Get or set the currently focused slide on a page using the focusedSlide property on PageNode.

```javascript
// Get the focused slide
const focused = figma.currentPage.focusedSlide;
if (focused) {
  return { focusedSlideId: focused.id, name: focused.name };
}

// Set the focused slide
const slide = figma.getNodeById("SLIDE_ID");
figma.currentPage.focusedSlide = slide;
```

--------------------------------

### Create OpenCode client and fetch sessions with Effect

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/sdk/README.md

Initializes OpenCode and retrieves a session using the Effect-native API from @opencode/sdk/effect.

```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/sdk/effect"

const opencode = yield * OpenCode.create()
const session = yield * opencode.sessions.get({ sessionID })
```

```bash
npm install @opencode-ai/sdk
```

### Build and package production release with CLI distribution

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/desktop/README.md

Build and package the desktop app for production using a specified prebuilt V2 CLI distribution path and channel.

```bash
OPENCODE_CHANNEL=prod OPENCODE_CLI_DIST=/absolute/path/to/packages/cli/dist bun run build
OPENCODE_CHANNEL=prod bun run package
```

### Install project dependencies

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/app/README.md

Installs the required package dependencies. While pnpm is used for repository templates, npm, pnpm, or yarn can be used interchangeably.

```bash
$ npm install # or pnpm install or yarn install
```

### Initial load and background plugin boot flow

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/specs/v2/catalog-config-plugin-lifecycle.md

Builds a baseline location layer from authored config and fast built-ins before activating slow background plugins and debouncing full-service reloads.

```ts
LocationServiceMap.get(ref)
  → build location layer
    → Config.layer reads authored documents
      → merge authored documents
      → run currently active Config transforms
    → Policy.layer reads transformed Config
    → Catalog.layer reads transformed Config
      → materialize baseline provider/model catalog
  → PluginBoot baseline ready
    → Frontend.fetchCatalog()

PluginBoot background fiber
  → install/update plugin packages concurrently
  → activate completed plugins
    → Config.transform()
      → transform(updateConfig)
    → ReloadScheduler.request()
      → debounce short burst of completed activations
      → Reload.all()
        → Config.get()
          → run newly active Config transforms
        → Catalog.reload()
          → Catalog.Event.Updated
            → Frontend.refetchCatalog()
```

### Run opencode serve with port, hostname, and CORS options

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/server.mdx

Starts the headless HTTP server. Use the optional flags to set the port, hostname, and allowed browser origins.

```bash
opencode serve [--port <number>] [--hostname <string>] [--cors <origin>]
```

```
